A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, mathematical expressions, and appendices. Retained content can be reliably matched despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original BoN and DPO experiments on Math Book and BiasQA, including numerical results and manual validation of its acknowledgment evaluator.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original results for another generator model, a disclaimer ablation, and CodeMMLU transfer evaluation.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same counterfactual prediction tests, strategies D and C, and disclaimer augmentation for BoN and DPO. v3 clarifies the evaluator's evaluation-only role and counterfactual sampling without establishing a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Math Book/AQUA-RAT and BiasQA/WINOGENERATED coverage is retained. v3 adds a limited software-reasoning transfer evaluation using 300 CodeMMLU Software Principles examples and Math Book-trained models (Appendix F, Table 4).

E2.justification: v3 adds RM_ALL, which appends disclaimers to every response, as an evaluated BoN comparator with both Skywork reward models (Appendix D, Figure 7). Existing base-model and default-RM comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v3 expands the evaluation design with full BoN/DPO experiments using Llama-3.2-3B, a blanket-disclaimer control, and cross-domain evaluation of Math Book-trained models. Appendix C also replaces classwise evaluator F1 reporting with macro-F1 and accuracy. Existing Llama-3.1-8B splits and training hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds a mechanism-focused ablation testing whether disclaimer wording alone explains mitigation (Figure 7), evaluator agreement and error examples (Tables 2–3), and a transfer analysis (Appendix F). These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence beyond v2's evaluator validation and generation examples.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three experiments with different seeds and report means and standard deviations. The additional results follow this existing practice; no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or increased run counts are reported.

E6.justification: v2 Tables 1–4 retain their numerical values in v3 Tables 1, 5, 6, and 9. v3 adds extensive 3B results, RM_ALL curves, transfer results, and revised evaluator metrics. For example, new Table 10 reports 3B BoN@16 stereotype rates of 68.1% with SK-Gemma-27B RM versus 55.5% with RM_C; these are new configurations, not improved earlier scores.

T1.justification: The prediction-disagreement criterion, unfaithfulness condition, and background BoN selection expression are retained. New diagrams and explanations introduce no substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain substantively unchanged: reward-guided optimization can promote unfaithful explanations, and causal-attribution augmentation can mitigate this behavior in controlled settings. Additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussion: the conclusion identifies controlled-setting limitations and difficulties constructing high-quality counterfactuals, while Section 5 explains D's label independence, C's proposed noise reduction, and avoidance of evaluator exploitation during training. Appendix F cautiously interprets mixed transfer evidence.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly documents exact-match answer extraction, invalid-output handling, and BoN counterfactual sampling from 16 responses. v3 also explicitly separates evaluator use from training. Existing DPO hyperparameters, hardware, software packages, prompt templates, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds comparison with Turpin et al. (2025), distinguishing pre-alignment generator training from alignment-stage RM augmentation and discussing possible complementarity. A CoT Monitorability paragraph and additional citations broaden context while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: The seven-section main narrative and much of the results prose remain. v3 makes localized rewrites and explanatory reorganizations, particularly in the introduction and Sections 3.2 and 5, revises appendix organization, and adds an LLM-usage statement.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main text from a two-column workshop layout to a single-column conference layout. It combines the introductory diagram with a reward-distribution panel, moves the original full distribution figure to Appendix B, adds counterfactual explanatory diagrams and experimental displays, and substantially rearranges appendix tables and plots.

improvement.justification: v2 lacked a control testing whether disclaimer wording alone explained mitigation. v3's RM_ALL experiment (Figure 7) addresses this important gap, strengthening support for selective causal attribution. Second-generator experiments, evaluator error examples, and explicit counterfactual limitations further improve credibility. Transfer evidence remains preliminary and mixed, and classwise evaluator F1 detail is lost, but the stronger validation of the central mechanism provides a substantial net improvement.
